title: Lumbar puncture in the febrile infant under 60 days
alt: Flowchart: an unwell febrile infant is resuscitated and given antibiotics, with the LP done once stable. A well-appearing infant is split by age: 7 days or less and 8 to 21 days always get an LP; 22 to 28 days gets an LP to decide about antibiotics; 29 to 60 days only if markers are abnormal or cultures positive. A contraindication defers the LP.
caption: Age bands and low-risk criteria follow the AAP 2021 guideline for well-appearing febrile infants 8–60 days; infants 7 days or less and unwell infants need a full sepsis evaluation.

nodes.text: Febrile infant under 60 days (38 °C or more)
Never delay antibiotics for the LP
Resuscitate, blood and urine cultures, IV antibiotics now; LP when stable
Age on the day of presentation?
Full sepsis evaluation including LP; admit on IV antibiotics
Blood, urine, CSF and inflammatory markers; LP in every infant; admit on IV antibiotics
Blood, urine, markers and LP; if markers normal, observe off antibiotics
Blood, urine and markers first; LP only if these are abnormal
No LP: no antibiotics, outpatient with review within 24 hours
Defer: unstable, signs of raised pressure, skin infection at the site, bleeding risk, shunt
Do the LP before the first antibiotic dose, or straight after it
Admit infants 28 days or less; antibiotics guided by CSF and culture results
